themes.consensus_view: The research reads Middle East supply disruption as still tightening the oil market and still pushing crude and fuel prices up, with Goldman Sachs and Société Générale taking that side and every other desk mention of the Strait of Hormuz staying descriptive rather than picking a direction.

facts_agreed.claim: Both banks that take a view treat the Middle East disruption as an ongoing tightening force on oil supply rather than one that is fading.
evidence_quotes: markets are increasingly pricing a prolonged Mideast conflict
product prices and especially cracks have risen to unprecedented levels relative to crude

facts_agreed.claim: Desk commentary consistently names the Strait of Hormuz as the specific chokepoint at risk, covering closure, blockade, shipping attacks and reopening.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy supply constraints

facts_agreed.claim: Desks also flag escalation of the conflict itself, not only the shipping route, as a live risk in this window.

themes.consensus_view: Goldman Sachs says orders for AI chips, servers and networking gear are still coming in faster than they can be filled, with power and physical datacenter buildout now the real bottleneck, while The Market Ear and Societe Generale push back that adoption is growing in a straight line rather than speeding up and that higher interest rates are shrinking what investors will pay for these stocks.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI compute is still running ahead of what suppliers can deliver, and none of the desks see orders rolling over.
evidence_quotes: demand continues to outpace supply, as evidenced by the growth in NBIS’s customer pipeline.
companies highlighted a strong AI spending environment with tight supply;
Compute demand rollover feels very difficult to argue.
The overall message from the conference presentations was decidedly bullish.

facts_agreed.claim: The binding constraint on the AI buildout has moved from finding customers to getting power and physical datacenter capacity in place.
evidence_quotes: From a policy perspective, the environment improves for the AI Power theme.
Physical infrastructure constraints for AI data centers
AI governance and power provision concerns

facts_agreed.claim: Agentic AI is a separate, newer source of demand for networking and compute capacity, not just more of the same training spend.
evidence_quotes: agentic AI is creating a multi-year networking supercycle
Agentic AI solutions to be a key driver of growth
DO views inference demand as inherently more durable than training

facts_agreed.claim: AI-linked stocks have pulled back from their highs and investor positioning has lightened.
evidence_quotes: Light positioning, a dramatic reset in implied vols and plenty of potential catalysts
The AI trade is well off recent highs and the backdrop is getting considerably more complicated.

facts_contested.claim: whether AI adoption is still accelerating or flattening into a linear grind
facts_contested.for_evidence: Compute demand rollover feels very difficult to argue.
facts_contested.against_evidence: Does that look like a 'rapid' adoption? Seems rather linear to us

facts_contested.claim: durability of the AI trade from current levels
facts_contested.for_evidence: AI fundamentals are strong and we have little concerns regarding expected returns.
facts_contested.against_evidence: The AI trade is well off recent highs and the backdrop is getting considerably more complicated.

facts_contested.claim: whether higher interest rates cap what AI and cloud infrastructure names are worth
facts_contested.for_evidence: cloud stocks are particularly sensitive to higher discount rates, which reduce the present value
facts_contested.against_evidence: AI fundamentals are strong and we have little concerns regarding expected returns.

themes.consensus_view: Goldman Sachs expects the Bank of Japan to raise its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18 and to keep raising slowly to 1.75% by July 2027, and five other desks treat Japanese rate increases as a live topic without anyone arguing the other side.

facts_agreed.claim: The desks treat further Bank of Japan rate increases as the working assumption, with Goldman Sachs naming September 18 as the date of the next one.
evidence_quotes: We maintain our forecast that the next BOJ policy rate hike will be on September 18

themes.consensus_view: Five desks treat the money big cloud companies are spending on AI hardware as a live subject this week, covering how fast the spending is rising, how much of it is borrowed, and what breaks if it stops, but none of them stakes out a directional call.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across several desks describe hyperscaler AI spending as an active and still-accelerating build cycle rather than a finished one.
The same desks flag how the buildout is being paid for and what it would cost if it reversed, referencing debt funding, credit repricing, an earnings drag and a burst scenario.

themes.consensus_view: Several bank desks reference an ongoing US-Iran military confrontation in the Gulf as live background for oil and risk markets, but none of them has staked a directional call on how it resolves.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks across four reports treat an active US-Iran military confrontation in the Gulf as ongoing background context, describing it variously as tanker, naval and Persian Gulf strike activity.
evidence_quotes: US-Iran strikes in the Persian Gulf

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree individual stocks are moving independently of each other and index-level swings are unusually small, which is keeping options unusually cheap, but they split on whether the calm lasts, with Societe Generale expecting it to persist while Goldman Sachs and The Market Ear are paying up for protection against its end.

facts_agreed.claim: Options on the index are cheap right now and worth owning for the payoff if the market starts moving again.
evidence_quotes: collect some cheap convexity when the market offers it to you.
convexity remains cheap. Long SPX straddles offer a clean two-sided expression

facts_agreed.claim: Individual stocks are moving apart from each other at historically low rates while single-stock price swings stay large, because a few dominant themes are pushing names in opposite directions.
evidence_quotes: Our base case is for the current configuration of high single stock volatility and low correlations to persist.
handful of powerful themes are pulling stocks in opposite directions, suppressing correlation and index volatility
Dispersion remains one of the most compelling structural themes.

facts_agreed.claim: The extra return investors demand for holding stocks over bonds has shrunk to about 2 percent, which makes equities more sensitive to moves in bond yields and keeps stocks and bonds selling off together.
evidence_quotes: shrinkage of Equity Risk Premia towards 2%, 100bp below historical averages
this positive correlation could be sustained both through a valuation channel

facts_contested.claim: whether the low-correlation, low-index-volatility regime persists
facts_contested.for_evidence: Our base case is for the current configuration of high single stock volatility and low correlations to persist.

themes.consensus_view: Four bank desks reference the US Treasury's program of buying back its own outstanding bonds as a live topic this window, and none of them takes a position on what it means for bond prices or yields.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks flag the US Treasury buyback operations as an active item this window without taking a side on the market impact.
Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale both single out the longer-dated part of the buyback program, including the 10 to 20 year maturity bucket.
